name: Immunodeficiency due to a complement cascade protein anomaly

criteria.description: Demonstration of decreased serum levels of one or more complement cascade proteins (e.g., C3, C4, C5-C9)
History of recurrent or severe infections with encapsulated bacteria such as Neisseria meningitidis
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes encoding complement cascade proteins
Normal immunoglobulin levels to exclude antibody deficiencies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of decreased serum complement protein levels plus recurrent invasive infections; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Complement function assays (CH50, AH50) are critical for functional assessment

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe invasive bacterial infections with encapsulated organisms
pathognomonic.notes: Includes pneumococcal and Haemophilus influenzae infections
searchTerms: severe infections with protective capsule bacteria
infections from bacteria with outer coating
low complement levels in blood test

common.symptomName: Recurrent episodes of meningitis or septicemia
Chronic or recurrent sinusitis and otitis media

common.notes: May be associated with complement consumption

occasional.symptomName: Autoimmune manifestations such as systemic lupus erythematosus-like symptoms
Chronic fatigue related to recurrent infections
searchTerms: persistent fatigue due to repeated infections
protein in urine from kidney inflammation

laboratory: Low serum levels of complement proteins (C3, C4, or terminal components C5-C9)
Reduced total hemolytic complement activity (CH50) or alternative pathway activity (AH50)
imaging: MRI or CT imaging may show complications of meningitis or abscess formation
Sinus imaging may reveal chronic sinusitis
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes encoding complement proteins (e.g., C3, C5, C6, C7, C8, C9)
Mutations in complement regulatory proteins (e.g., factor H, factor I) may be identified
other: Positive blood cultures with Neisseria species during infections
Complement functional assays essential for diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Low immunoglobulin levels rather than complement deficiency
Frequent sinopulmonary infections but less Neisserial infections
Defect in phagocyte NADPH oxidase causing impaired oxidative burst
Recurrent catalase-positive bacterial and fungal infections

redFlags: Severe infections with encapsulated bacteria despite normal immunoglobulins
Family history of complement deficiency or early severe infections
references: Orphanet: Immunodeficiency due to complement cascade protein anomaly, ORPHA:101992

Tangye SG, Al-Herz W, Bousfiha A, et al. Human Inborn Errors of Immunity: 2019 Update on the Classification from the International Union of Immunological Societies Expert Committee. J Clin Immunol. 2020
